> Operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are not executed when building the vignette because they require the project data.

# Why assess the result?

Algorithm termination does not imply that all records are correct. Step 11
compares original and corrected data, uses the final extended-DAG routing check
stored in the correction result, and produces a quality report. It also uses
the initial check, exact donor records, elapsed time and donor provenance when
available.

```{r report-step}
source(file.path("scripts", "11_correction_quality_report.R"))
```

The script reads `correction_result.rds` and
`corrected_questionnaire_data.rds` from Step 10, together with
`prepared_data_with_logical_edits.rds` and `questionnaire_extended_DAG.rds`
from Step 09. It produces `correction_quality_report.rds`, an HTML report and
CSV tables in `correction_quality_output_dir`, or in the `quality-report`
subdirectory of the correction output directory.

# Reading the report

| Question | Evidence to inspect |
|:--|:--|
| How many records are resolved? | Record summary, separating resolved and unresolved cases |
| Do any violations remain? | Initial and final reports by record and variable |
| Which values changed? | Change tables and breakdown by change type |
| Were donors admissible? | Provenance and diagnostics of the EXACT pool |
| Were constrained variables respected? | Audit of immutable variables and exogenous auxiliary variables |
| What is the computational cost? | Elapsed time and execution summary |

Assess the resolution rate separately from persistent errors. A record may
remain unresolved; do not classify it as corrected merely because a value
changed. Retain complete outputs and pilot settings to reproduce comparisons.

# Selecting the result to assess

Step 11 must not inadvertently use the default pilot directory after a run
was saved elsewhere. Use the same output directory as Step 10 and the same
original extended data. Run this example from the project root:

```{r quality-config, eval=FALSE}
pkgload::load_all(".", export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE)
run <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source("scripts/00_config.R", envir = run)
run$config$correction_output_dir <- "output/corrected-full-STRATUM"
run$config$correction_quality_output_dir <- file.path(
  run$config$correction_output_dir, "quality-report"
)
run$correction_quality_report <- SSPICE::correction_quality_report
run$`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x
sys.source("scripts/11_correction_quality_report.R", envir = run)
```

The function uses `final_check` when supplied, otherwise
`correction_result$final_routing_check`. It does not automatically run a new,
independent validation of the final dataset. The script may, however,
recompute the initial check if neither a configured nor a saved check is found.

# Interpreting the counts

`records_resolved` measures constraint resolution, not the statistical accuracy
of imputation relative to unknown true values. `records_changed` includes
modified records even if they remain unresolved. `fills`, `blanks` and
`mode_changes` distinguish missing-to-value, value-to-missing and
value-to-different-value transitions, respectively. The percentage of changed
cells uses the `editable_cells` denominator calculated by the report, not all
cells in the original questionnaire.

Quantitative/qualitative classifications are inferred from routing metadata
and the classes of the prepared columns. Text may already have been converted
to indicators: `string_variables = 0` does not show that the original
questionnaire contained no open-ended questions. A numeric identifier can be
classified as quantitative while retaining the separate RECORD_ID role.

When comparing runs, retain inputs, seed, controls, donors and immutable
variables. Changing the stratification variable with `freeze_strata = TRUE`
also changes the automatically frozen variable. Similar change counts do not
imply identical imputed values. Compare correction time separately from total
elapsed time and cache reuse.

## Territorial stratum codes

In the supplied example, STRATUM identifies five geographical
divisions of Italy: North-West (1), North-East (2), Centre (3),
South (4), and Islands (5). It is used for stratification during
correction. With freeze_strata = TRUE, stratum membership remains
unchanged.
